title: Capacity stewardship cadence and SLO portfolio alignment
author: Amina Patel
content:
Overview

This document prescribes a repeatable cross-functional cadence for capacity stewardship that ensures the SLO portfolio is aligned with real capacity supply and business priorities. It focuses on continuous reconciliation of SLOs, error budgets, and multi-tenant capacity allocation (headroom) so teams can make predictable trade-offs between cost, latency, and availability.

Goals

- Maintain >=95% confidence that committed SLOs are achievable given current capacity commitments and forecasted demand.
- Detect and remediate SLO drift and error-budget consumption early (target detection within 24 hours of significant change).
- Provide a predictable, auditable cadence for capacity reallocation and non-disruptive migration of tenant traffic.

Scope and audience

This is intended for SREs, product/platform owners, and service stewards responsible for inference-serving and multi-tenant routing. Applies to hosted API, Dedicated pools, and Private deployments where central capacity governance is required.

Key concepts and definitions

- SLO portfolio: the set of active SLOs (latency, availability, correctness) across services that are eligible for central capacity stewardship.
- Error budget: remaining fraction of SLO slack for a lookback window (typically 30d); used as the operational currency for throttles/rollouts.
- Headroom: reserved capacity buffer (expressed in GPU-minutes or RPS-calc) to absorb short-term demand spikes without violating SLOs.
- Stewardship window: the recurrent meeting where stewards reconcile portfolio health and allocate headroom (see Cadence).

Stewardship cadence (calendar)

1) Daily: Automated health pass (SRE automation)
- What runs: portfolio telemetry pipeline computes a daily "Stewardship Snapshot" by 06:00 UTC.
- Outputs: list of services with >5% 24h jump in burn-rate, tail-latency regressions beyond configured thresholds, and any new error budget alarms.
- Owners: telemetry pipeline (sre-observability) writes to #sre-capacity-alerts and issues an automatic ticket for services crossing critical thresholds.

2) Weekly: Triage & short-term allocation (SRE + product stewards)
- Objective: triage items surfaced by daily snapshots and perform one-week capacity trades.
- Attendees: SRE oncall steward, product steward(s), runtime performance owner.
- Agenda (30 minutes): review top-5 consuming services, approve emergency capacity grants (max 15% of pool), schedule deeper investigations.
- Output: annotated authorization in the capacity ledger and an action ticket with owner and SLAs for remediation.

3) Monthly: Capacity reconciliation and forecasting (SRE platform + finance)
- Objective: reconcile observed headroom usage vs. forecast, adjust reserve targets, and identify upcoming model rollouts that require provisioning.
- Inputs: 30d telemetry, 90d forecast from product teams, reserved capacity utilization metrics.
- Deliverables: updated headroom target per pool, prioritized provisioning request list, finance impact estimate.

4) Quarterly: SLO portfolio review and admission policy refresh (cross-functional)
- Objective: review SLOs for business alignment, retire/modify low-value SLOs, and update admission rules for new tenants.
- Attendees: SRE leads, product managers, platform engineering, customer success for at-risk enterprise tenants.
- Deliverables: SLO change proposals, revised admission thresholds, and rollout plan for any SLO changes.

Decision matrix: When to grant capacity vs. require optimization

- Emergency grant (auto-approved at weekly triage): services with >50% 24h burn rate increase attributable to traffic (not regressions). Grant limit: 15% pool capacity for 72 hours.
- Short-term grant (requires steward sign-off): for planned campaigns or model experiments lasting <=14 days. Grant limit: up to 30% pool with documented rollback plan.
- No grant / require optimization: services with persistent error-budget burn due to non-traffic regressions (code/quantization). Action: require remediation and capacity-neutral rollout.

SLO and error-budget thresholds (recommended baseline)

| Tier | Typical SLO | Error-budget policy | Headroom target (pool %) | Escalation window |
|------|-------------|---------------------|--------------------------|------------------|
| Platinum | 99.95% availability / p99 latency SLA | Auto-grant only for verified region incidents; reserve 20% headroom | 25 | 1h |
| Gold | 99.9% / p95 latency target | Weekly steward approval for short grants; finance notification above 10% cost delta | 15 | 4h |
| Standard | 99.5% / median latency | Must optimize before capacity increase; can request experiments | 8 | 24h |

(Represent table in Confluence as above; values are guidance and must be adapted per pool.)

Operational signals and alert thresholds

- Burn-rate anomaly: relative change > 5x baseline burn-rate over 6h -> severity P2 alert.
- Tail-latency delta: p99 latency regression > 20% over 12h -> P2.
- Error budget remaining < 30% -> P3 advisory; <10% -> P1 immediate review.
- Headroom utilization > 80% -> P1 capacity planning alert.

Sample telemetry queries

- Prometheus (tail latency):
  sum(rate(request_duration_seconds_bucket{job="inference-runtime",le="1.0"}[5m])) by (service) / sum(rate(request_duration_seconds_count{job="inference-runtime"}[5m])) by (service)

- BigQuery (error budget burn):
  SELECT service, SUM(tokens) as tokens_consumed, SUM(CASE WHEN status != 'ok' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) as errors
  FROM `redwood-prod.telemetry.tokens_v2`
  WHERE event_time BETWEEN TIMESTAMP_SUB(CURRENT_TIMESTAMP(), INTERVAL 30 DAY) AND CURRENT_TIMESTAMP()
  GROUP BY service

Ownership and roles

- Steward (primary): maintains the capacity ledger, chairs weekly triage, approves short grants.
- Service steward (per-service): responsible for remediation, SLO proposals, and forecasting.
- Capacity platform: implements grants, runs autoscaling, and enforces quota guards.
- Finance liaison: validates cost impact for quarterly provisioning.

Runbook excerpts: emergency headroom exhaustion

1) Trigger: headroom utilization > 90% for two consecutive 15m windows or error budget < 5%.
2) Immediate actions (first 15 minutes):
   - Declare "Capacity Alert" in incident tooling and notify #sre-capacity-ops.
   - Identify top 3 services by allocation using the capacity ledger query.
   - Execute automated soft-throttle on non-critical tenants (pre-authorized lists).
3) Next actions (15-60 minutes):
   - Approve emergency grant (if traffic-driven and within limits) or escalate to oncall SRE lead.
   - If grant not approved, activate degraded routing policy (route to smaller models, reduce max tokens).
4) Post-incident (within 72 hours):
   - Produce a stewardship post-incident note: cause, mitigation, capacity changes, and recommendations for future prevention.

Templates and artifacts

- Capacity ledger entry (example fields): service, pool, requested-gpu-minutes, rationale, approved-by, expiry, rollback-plan.
- Stewardship Snapshot (automated): service, burn_rate_30d, burn_rate_24h, headroom_pct, error_budget_remaining, p99_latency_change.
- Monthly reconciliation template: forecast delta table, finance impact, provisioning plan.

Practical guidance and anti-patterns

- Prefer optimization before buying capacity: a 10% tail-latency reduction often yields more headroom than a 10% capacity add.
- Do not use error budget as permanent capacity justification. Recurrent high burn rates require root cause fixes and potential SLO re-evaluation.
- Avoid manual, undocumented temporary grants. All grants must be logged in the ledger with expiry.

Related policies and pages

- See service-onboarding-runway-and-slo-admission-playbook for admission criteria and templates.
- See slo-rollout-readiness-and-capacity-checklist for pre-deployment checks.

Appendix: common CLI commands and queries

- Create a ledger entry (example):
  curl -X POST https://capacity-api.internal/v1/ledger -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' -d '{"service":"vision-infer","pool":"dedicated-east","requested_gpu_min":3600,"expiry":"2026-03-01T00:00:00Z"}'

- Check headroom by pool (Prometheus example):
  sum(avg_over_time(gpu_utilization{pool="dedicated-east"}[1h])) by (pool)

Feedback and iteration

This cadence is expected to evolve. Submit suggested changes via the stewardship RFC process (label: capacity-rfc). For initial adoption, we recommend a 90-day pilot on one dedicated pool to validate thresholds and tooling integration.
